sequence.label: C1-T0
sequence.prompt:
Our town library is reviewing its reservation service. Members search the catalogue, choose a title, and join a waiting list when every copy is on loan. Staff contact the next member when a returned copy becomes available. Reserved books remain at the collection desk for three working days. Members can update their contact details through an online account. The service sends email reminders before a reservation expires. Staff help members who cannot use the website and record telephone reservations in the same queue. Each title has its own waiting list ordered by reservation time. A member can cancel a reservation without losing a place on another list. The library wants shorter waiting times and fewer uncollected books. Its budget allows small changes to messages and staff procedures, but no additional building or large software purchase. Staff will review outcomes weekly using reservation counts, cancellations, and collection delays. The manager plans a small pilot before changing the entire service. One volunteer will check reminder messages and another will record whether members collect books on time. Every week the team will compare the number of notices sent, cancelled reservations, and books returned to the shelf. They will ask members whether the messages are clear and whether collection hours are convenient. Changes must preserve the original order of the waiting list and provide the same service to telephone and online members. 
Give a brief summary. Note 1.0.
